[USER] User asked about the Euclidean distance between two points (a,b) and (x,y).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The Euclidean distance between two points (a,b) and (x,y) is given by the formula: sqrt((x-a)^2 + (y-b)^2).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The formula is derived from the Pythagorean theorem.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Example coordinates provided: (3,4) and (6,8).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Calculation example: sqrt((6-3)^2 + (8-4)^2) = sqrt(9 + 16) = sqrt(25) = 5.  
[USER] User asked for the integral of 1/x for x=1 to x=2.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The indefinite integral of 1/x is given by the formula: ln |x| + C, where C is a constant.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] To find the definite integral of 1/x from x=1 to x=2, evaluate: integral from x=1 to x=2 of (1/x) dx = ln |2| - ln |1|.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Result of the definite integral: ln 2.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The definite integral of 1/x from x=1 to x=2 is equal to ln 2.
